abbreviation_curriculum.scope: attested Cyrillic abbreviations of this split's share, typed as written after Russian prose, labelled by the term counts of both readings (abbreviation_curriculum).

capital_citation_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: keep frames of Latin capitals after Russian prose whose Cyrillic reading is a rare lexicon word (capital_citation_curriculum).

english_capital_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: keep frames of the keys of common Russian words typed in Latin capitals after English prose (english_capital_curriculum).

joined_token_curriculum.scope: words joined by hyphens in the text of this split's rows, and counted words of either language joined to themselves, after the text before them: typed as written (keep) and their keys in the other layout (convert) (joined_token_curriculum).

kept_neighbour_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: kept_next_word frames, the question a waiting word is asked again with its kept next word (kept_neighbour_curriculum).

latin_abbreviation_curriculum.scope: attested Cyrillic abbreviations of this split's share, typed as written after English prose or Latin terms, labelled by the term counts of both readings (latin_abbreviation_curriculum).

letter_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: a word of one letter after a counted technical term in Russian sentences and in place of a word of English ones, at its boundary and beside its next word (letter_curriculum).

portable.scope: TRAIN only: three-letter words of the pinned lexicons and the shipped identifier index whose other reading is a real word or command too, standing alone with the deferred label and with planned variants labelled convert; words of this corpus's test and of every accessed test are refused by their aliases.

reference_hunspell.scope: TRAIN only: three-letter words of the pinned lexicons and the shipped identifier index whose other reading is a real word or command too, standing alone with the deferred label and with planned variants labelled convert; words of this corpus's test and of every accessed test are refused by their aliases.

calibration.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

development.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

train.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

calibration.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

development.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

train.scope: lone_word frames of this split: every pair of two Latin letters whose Russian keys are letters too, each reading alone in the field at a boundary other than a space (lone_word_curriculum), labelled by alone_labels with the frozen model's answer where the counts settle nothing.

portable.scope: Old TRAIN annotations and first words of their existing right contexts; no new split or candidate context-model labels.

reference_hunspell.scope: Old TRAIN annotations and first words of their existing right contexts; no new split or candidate context-model labels.

calibration.scope: Natural short typing frames of one split paired with the first word of their own sentence's continuation; no cross-split anchors and no candidate context-model labels.

development.scope: Natural short typing frames of one split paired with the first word of their own sentence's continuation; no cross-split anchors and no candidate context-model labels.

train.scope: Natural short typing frames of one split paired with the first word of their own sentence's continuation; no cross-split anchors and no candidate context-model labels.

portable.policy: planned frames per (direction, focus length) carry the total mass of the isolated deferred frames of the same class

reference_hunspell.policy: planned frames per (direction, focus length) carry the total mass of the isolated deferred frames of the same class

abbreviation_curriculum.scope: TRAIN, and DEVELOPMENT for the head's epoch (one form in ABBREVIATION_SPLIT_MODULUS by hash): every Cyrillic word of two to five letters of the term table in capitals whose Latin reading is letters too, typed as written after frames_per_form left contexts of Russian rows of the split; convert when the Latin reading is counted at least minimum_latin_count times and dominance times as often, keep otherwise (tools/train_context_action_model.abbreviation_curriculum).

recipe.acceptance_note: A model is judged by what it nets: conversions it gets right minus conversions it gets wrong, in each deployment profile. The zero-false-conversion budget was removed on 17.09.2026 together with the class-wide runtime vetoes it depended on; the sealed test still requires no more corrupted text than the installed pair and a net result at least as good.

capital_citation_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: the keys of rare Russian words of the portable lexicon (three to five letters, counted fewer than five times in Russian text, none written in capitals by the onboard lexicon) typed in the Latin layout in capitals - the shape of a cited Latin abbreviation such as `WBC` (`ЦИС`) or `IBF` (`ШИА`) - stand after the left context of a Russian TRAIN row, chosen by hash, labelled keep, and the same keys in lower case in the same frame labelled convert (the Russian word typed in the wrong layout), so the pair tells case apart rather than teaching that Latin after Russian prose stays; no convert frame for their Cyrillic reading, which may be the writer's own abbreviation. Words held by this corpus's test or any accessed test are refused by their aliases. Natural rows of every split with such a Latin word get one keep frame after Russian prose too (mixed-capital). Motivation: the corpus v22 candidate and the baseline pair converted `по версии WBC` into `ЦИС` on test v22 with the early switch off; natural TRAIN held 17 such rows. Without the lower-case pair (corpus v23, 400 words) the candidate missed 9 more of the owner's words than the same recipe without the curriculum, nearly all short lower-case Latin keys of Russian words after Russian text (`f` for `а`, `lkz` for `для`).

captured_curriculum.scope: Not used: maximum_rows_per_source 0 leaves the captured questions out of TRAIN; the corpus and its curricula alone. Measured 03.10.2026 on corpus v17 with the line, opening and term-frequency evidence, against the private replay of the owner's own typing: the questions at half weight with 30% convert, at full weight with 50% convert, and without the questions about the first word of a line each converted Russian abbreviations into Latin less often, but missed more of the words the owner corrected by hand (49-50 against 42 without them) and the first two kept short words opening a message as typed (`ns`, `Lf`); model/context_v3/README.md.

counted_token_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: the word decided at its own boundary (after_origin none). Russian abbreviations the term table counts in Russian technical text at least minimum_abbreviation_count times and abbreviation_dominance times as often as their Latin keys (`тз`, not `зк`), no lexicon word, typed as intended after the left context of a Russian row, keep; Latin terms counted at least minimum_term_count times whose Cyrillic reading is nothing, typed in the Russian layout in the same place, convert; three frames for every such term and abbreviation (the budgets cover both classes whole: a candidate that framed 800 of the 1752 terms and all 802 abbreviations kept `тз` but missed `тзь` for `npm`), the boundaries of the capital citations. Motivation: the corpus v27 candidate converted `тз` to `np` (p=0.993), `2фа`, `кз` and `ви` in the owner's typing while the token's count pulled the other way without a frame to learn from (tools/train_context_action_model.counted_token_curriculum). Not used while a frozen base is named: its frames moved the shared frequency features, and the `ша` before `hello` stayed `ша` (corpus v27 and v28 candidates).

english_capital_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: the keys of the Russian lexicon's commonest words of two to five letters (all 107 two-letter ones the keys spell in Latin letters), typed in the Latin layout in capitals, after the left context of an English TRAIN row whose words are all Latin, chosen by hash, two contexts a word - keep, and the same keys in lower case in the same frame - convert (without that pair the first corpus v29 candidates left 31 more of the owner's Russian words typed in the Latin layout as typed: `yt`, `yf`, `rfr`, `xnj`). Motivation: test v28 holds two Latin capitals inside an English sentence whose keys spell `из`, and the corpus v26 pair turned them into `ИЗ` (p=0.997, reference lexicons, early switch off): Latin capitals had been framed after Russian prose only (tools/train_context_action_model.english_capital_curriculum).

epoch_selection.calibration: independent final serving-threshold selection after weights are selected, never below the development operating threshold of the selected epoch: a threshold that already converted falsely on development is not a serving candidate whatever calibration says
epoch_selection.rounding: nine decimal places before development prediction
epoch_selection.serving_threshold_floor: development operating threshold of the selected epoch

frozen_base.scope: The corpus v37 model (context-v3-2ae75d2b9e38, 0.44.0) with every weight fixed: the word decided at its boundary, the kept-neighbour question and the capitals, lone-word, message-start, single-letter and abbreviation heads it carries. The lone-word head's frames are labelled with the counts it was fitted with (carried.alone). The Latin-context abbreviation head is fitted onto it: a Cyrillic abbreviation in capitals that Russian technical text uses, after Latin text (context_action_features.latin_abbreviation_question), with how often each reading occurs in Russian and technical text and in English prose and how often the word before it does. Motivation: the owner's typing of 08.10.2026, where `/designv2 ТЗ` became `/designv2 NP`. The unknown-token head is fitted onto it too: a token of four or more letters (and digits) of one script, not all capitals, whose Cyrillic reading Russian prose does not use and whose typed reading no lexicon of its layout holds, after Russian text - Latin letters in either layout, Russian letters only when the text before already holds their Latin reading as a word (context_action_features.unknown_question) - with the shared features once more and, per layout, whether either reading occurs earlier in the text, whether a reading is one typo from a word, and the length. Motivation: the owner's typing of 13.10.2026 in a chat input of VS Code, where `цуиоы` stayed for `webjs` four times, twice after `webjs` typed right earlier, and the row test v56 lost: the last word of a short Russian message, a word no table counts, typed in the English layout. The joined-token head is fitted onto it too: a token one of whose readings is words joined by hyphens (context_action_features.joined_question), with how often the most and the least frequent word of each reading occurs in its language's prose and whether the token repeats one word; the shared features read no count of such a token. Motivation: sealed test v58, where `Re-re!` after a Russian sentence, meant as `Ку-ку!`, stayed with both pairs: no term table counts such a token.

identifier_lexicon.evidence: source_identifier and target_identifier flags from exact case-insensitive membership; feature identifier:{source}:{target}, and only when a reading is an identifier its combinations with direction, length and left-context script (identifier:0:0 combinations would duplicate existing evidence), plus source:identifier and target:identifier
identifier_lexicon.scope: Debian trixie main amd64 executable names, the same index the technical corpus was frozen from; a resource shared byte-for-byte by engine, trainer and evaluator, not a training split. Calibration and test technical rows measure commands present in the shipped index; identifiers outside it are measured by the lexicon-blind development diagnostic and are not gated.

training_dropout.scope: TRAIN only: one family in three (a command with all its contexts and spelling variants; otherwise the row), chosen by the corpus variant hash of the family key with purpose identifier-dropout, is featurised with an empty identifier lexicon, so command-like strings outside the shipped index keep converting on their own evidence. Development, calibration and test always use the full lexicon.

joined_token_curriculum.scope: Every token of words of one script joined by hyphens in the text of the split's rows, at most four occurrences of one token, and 400 words of each language that its prose counts five times or more, of two to four letters, each joined to itself (half of them opening a sentence with a capital), after the text before them: typed as written (keep) and their keys typed in the other layout (convert). Its DEVELOPMENT copy chooses the head's own epoch, and the other heads' shared epoch is chosen without the head's weights: ranked with them, its frames moved that epoch to where the unknown-token head lost a word of the owner's typing. The interjections of the authored battery that gates the head are held out.

joint_acceptance.policy: A context candidate is accepted only together with an explicit prefix candidate: the candidate pair is replayed against the frozen baseline context plus the frozen baseline prefix under unmodified application defaults (early switch, pause correction, manual-layout protection) and under the previous early-off control. Every sequence gate must hold in both modes and both lexical profiles. Installed context and prefix bytes are never read by the evaluation; the joint receipt records both evaluated artifacts so packaging installs exactly those bytes.

kept_neighbour_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: the question a waiting word is asked again beside its next word, which stayed as typed (after_origin kept_next_word, features under KEPT_FEATURE_PREFIX with their own budget). Natural short words of either language with the sentence's next word keep; Latin terms the term table counts in Russian technical text, typed in the Russian layout before the word of a Russian row, convert; frequent Russian abbreviations and misspelt Russian words in the same place keep (tools/train_context_action_model.kept_neighbour_curriculum).

latin_abbreviation_curriculum.scope: TRAIN, and DEVELOPMENT for the head's epoch (the abbreviation curriculum's share of forms): every Cyrillic word of two to five letters of the term table in capitals whose Latin reading is letters too, typed as written after frames_per_form left contexts, in turn of an English row of the split and of one or two Latin terms counted at least minimum_term_count times; keep when the Cyrillic word is counted at least minimum_cyrillic_count times and dominance times as often as its Latin reading among the Latin words of Russian technical text or in English prose, whichever is more, convert otherwise (tools/train_context_action_model.latin_abbreviation_curriculum).

recipe.legacy_variant_policy: Preserve semantic fields and completed-word lookahead. Each original family/category/trigger has unit pre-class mass shared equally across its actions, then equally across variants of that action.

letter_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: a Russian TRAIN sentence's word of one letter (а и в с к у о я) with the word before it replaced by a Latin term Russian technical text counts at least minimum_term_count times and at least as often as English prose does (or the term alone before it, one sentence in three); typed in the English layout the letter waits at its boundary and converts beside its next word, converted or kept as typed (another term); typed as written it keeps. An English TRAIN sentence's word between two words replaced by the Latin keys of one of those letters waits and keeps beside its next word; an English word of one letter keeps at its boundary and beside it (tools/train_context_action_model.letter_curriculum).

lexical_short_pair_curriculum.scope: TRAIN only: every three-letter word of the pinned onboard lexicons and the shipped identifier index whose other reading is a real word or command too (tools/train_context_action_model.py lexical_short_pairs; supplement-only forms are never a conversion target), standing alone in both readings with the deferred label and, per reading, LEXICAL_PAIR_ANCHOR_VARIANTS planned_next_conversion variants with words of the split's own right contexts labelled convert, one unit of mass per reading. Natural text holds almost no such pair (corpus v12 TRAIN: 21 rows in 45 544), so the corpus v13 candidate trained without it had no convert-labelled planned frame for a Latin three-letter word and kept `tot` after a converted `привет`. Words of this corpus's test and of every accessed test are refused by the same aliases the fitting extension refuses.

lexicon_supplement.name: opensubtitles-2018-ru-full-min10-outside-onboard-v2
lexicon_supplement.scope: Cyrillic forms of the pinned OpenSubtitles 2018 full Russian frequency list with list count >= 10 absent from the frozen onboard ru_RU.lm vocabulary (199,680 forms; v1 was the top-50k list, 27 209 forms). The count floor is a noise bound chosen from the list itself before any fit: samples at counts 1-9 still carry one-off misspellings and transliterations, loaded as extra known forms with the fallback frequency by LanguageModel.load and by the trainers' reference models alike; a lexical resource, not a training split. Motivation: correctly typed colloquial words, interjections and transliterated names unknown to the portable lexicon were the class behind the isolated short-token deferrals and the residual convert-vs-keep confusions.

recipe.lookahead_policy: Replace bounded old TRAIN short-space seeds with original/planned variants of equal total mass. Positives retain annotated next words; KEEP negatives retain their original/before annotation with an explicitly mixed existing TRAIN anchor. A frozen lexical baseline proposal is an entry condition, not a label. No candidate context-model prediction selects labels.
recipe.mixed_insertion_policy: Every natural row frames both readings of its word as an insertion into prose of the other language with the fixed phrases of MIXED_INSERTION_CONTEXTS (one of them cites the word in a parenthesis after a quoted name). Since corpus v18 a citation-shaped Latin word - capitalised, upper-case or unknown to the portable lexicon and the identifier index - whose Cyrillic reading is no Russian word is framed once more after the left context of a real Russian row of the same split, chosen by hash, when that context has words and all of them are Cyrillic: the Latin reading keeps, the Cyrillic reading converts. The base treebanks are monolingual (corpus v13 TRAIN: 130 Latin rows after Russian text among 18 363), while encyclopedic prose cites Latin names and abbreviations constantly; the v15 candidate left an abbreviation of three capitals and a capitalised name typed in the Russian layout as typed on test v13. Framing every word of both languages that way (corpus v16) taught that any Latin token after a Russian clause may be an insertion and that `чем` after Russian prose is the command its Latin keys spell; framing every citation-shaped Latin word (corpus v17) still held `ns` after `мы решили, что ` at p=0.983, because `ns` is an unknown Latin token whose Cyrillic reading, `ты`, is the word meant. Since corpus v20 each such citation is framed once more with an opening sign typed in the Latin layout (two backticks, an apostrophe or a double quote, chosen by hash), because those keys are the letters ёё, э and Э in the Russian layout and the Cyrillic reading of the whole token is letters only: the corpus v19 candidate converted two backtick-opened capitalised Latin citations after Russian prose on test v15 that the baseline pair kept. Since corpus v24 one Russian row in four (QUOTE_TAIL_MODULUS, chosen by hash) is framed once more closing a quotation with its quote typed in the layout of the word: the Russian reading with `"` keeps, its keys in the Latin layout (`ghbdtn@`: the Russian `"` is the `@` key) convert. The corpus splits the quote off as a token of its own, and every corpus v23 candidate left `ghbdtn@` as typed with the early switch off. Since corpus v24 a row whose previous word reads as a word in the other layout (two letters or more) is framed once more with that previous word as typed in the other layout and the row's word typed there too, labelled convert: a phrase typed whole in the wrong layout leaves behind exactly the word whose wrong reading is a word (`here` is `руку`), and the next word is still the phrase's (`руку ерун` is `here they`); natural frames only ever followed correctly typed text.

natural_lookahead_curriculum.scope: Every split separately (train, development, calibration): natural deferrable space-boundary frames of a document are seeds (one- and two-letter words, and three-letter words whose two readings are both plausible, the words the engine may hold for their next word), the first word of the same row's own sentence continuation is the anchor, and the observed/empty variants divide their mass between the original frame and a planned_next_conversion variant, so field-start lookahead is trained, selected and calibrated on the same evidence the engine builds. Anchors never cross a split.

recipe.natural_tail_policy: direct-boundary natural frames have empty segmented tails; supplementary physical spans provide actual engine tails and preceding whitespace in train/development/calibration
recipe.planned_mass_policy: TRAIN only, after both lookahead curricula: per (direction, focus length of 1 or 2) the planned_next_conversion frames are rescaled to carry exactly the total mass of the isolated deferred (wait/suggest, no word on either side) frames of the same class. The two are the same physical moment seen before and after the next word is known; legacy parent budgets alone left the planned regime at about one hundredth of that mass and the model could not learn the after-context distinction (planned `у этого` stayed below the serving threshold in exp05-exp08). Development and calibration frames are never rescaled.

model_verdict_stands.removed: unlicensed_isolated and short_uppercase_unknown_source, both class-wide vetoes, were removed on 17.09.2026: they overruled the model on the input it was trained to tell apart, cost 14 of 300 restorations on chat-like first words and prevented no corruption (.t/reliable-release-2026-09-12/SHORT-ISOLATED-CURRICULUM.md). The earlier short_unknown_source entry named the same ban from the training side and is gone with it.
model_verdict_stands.rule: The model's verdict decides. This layer refuses nothing for a class of input; a conversion is refused only by an exception the user can see - an excluded word or application, their own switching settings, a rule they taught the engine - or by the model's own calibrated threshold. A suggestion - the model leaning to the other layout below its threshold - converts when the detector converts the word too, a lone letter excepted (ContextPolicy.decide, 13.10.2026): two verdicts of the same direction; the model's keep and wait stand.

recipe.short_pair_policy: Both readings of an isolated token share WAIT/SUGGEST when neither neighbour contains a word and the token's intent is not observable: any token of at most two letters (the curated single letters aside), and a token of three letters whose two readings are both plausible - a known word of the portable lexicon of its layout or a shipped identifier each (tools/context_deferral.py; `tot`/`еще`, `зум`/the Debian command `pev`). A three-letter token with one plausible reading is labelled at once (`rjn`/`кот`, `три`), and one with none is left to the model's own evidence (`зь2`/`pm2`). Digits and punctuation alone are not a language label. Historical KEEP frames of such isolated tokens take the same deferred action, so natural and legacy frames never label one observable situation differently; historical CONVERT frames keep their declared label.
recipe.span_policy: fixed-hash families and same-split anchors; literal suffix and repeated-space variants; exact captured parent body and counterfactual full-prefix labels; one pre-class sample unit per retained family

threshold_selection.ceiling_rule: The served threshold stays inside the band the product's own pinned cases define, which are open data and never a sealed test. Measured 18.09.2026: it must clear the cases that have to stay as typed - `лут` against the command name `ken` at 0.9887 and `Вас` against `Dfc` at 0.9889 - and it must not exceed the tightest case that has to convert, the idle correction of `rjn` to `кот` at 0.994424. Calibration counts rows and can see neither end: outside the band it picks a model that is careless on one side or cautious about the wrong thing on the other.
threshold_selection.rule: Among the thresholds whose calibration balance is within the tolerance of the best, serve the one with the fewest false conversions, the lowest such threshold on a tie. The balance decides which thresholds are admissible; within a plateau of equal value the safer point is served, because the two sides are not equally sensitive to it - on corpus v12 (18.09.2026) moving from 0.95 to 0.995 gave up 0.8 % of the correct conversions and removed two thirds of the false ones.

recipe.training_order: SHA256 of frame identifiers mixes natural and legacy rows deterministically

unknown_token_curriculum.scope: TRAIN, and DEVELOPMENT for the head's epoch (one term in five by hash): one in item_modulus of the Latin tokens of letters and digits the term table counts at least minimum_term_count times whose keys in the Russian layout are a token of the unknown-token head's shape that no lexicon holds and Russian prose does not use, after the left context of a Russian row: typed in the Russian layout with the term typed right earlier in the text (convert), and typed as meant (keep), for one term in echo_modulus also after itself and after its Cyrillic keys; and one in echo_modulus of the head's Russian words of the split's own rows with their keys earlier in the text (keep). TRAIN families of five letters or more drop their own term counts one time in three. The held_out tokens are those of the authored batteries that gate the head (tools/train_context_action_model.unknown_token_curriculum).

recipe.variant_policy: separate SHA256 streams for trigger, application, optional field-after and boundary event
recipe.vocabulary_policy: Kahan-summed pre-class sample mass; presence only; cutoff tolerance 1e-9; mass rounded to 9 decimal places for ranking ties

scope: natural KEEP plus declared layout/mixed-context interventions; sequence evaluation required

unknown_token_curriculum.scope: terms of the Latin table typed in the Russian layout after Russian prose (convert), some with the term typed right earlier in the text, and the class's Russian words of the split's rows with their keys earlier in the text (keep), of this split's share (unknown_token_curriculum).
